evidence: Audit Q41 confirms primary pass, whole fail: generation already silences the old button; the rewrite adds dual cleanup that could clear a newer binding and its negative-only test passes the original code.
reviewProposal: Grade primary (old target silent, current dispatches), regression risk (teardown cannot clear a newer binding), rework, and evidence (require a positive current-dispatch assertion before asserting the old one is silent) separately.

evidence: Audit Q25: primary pass (main code keeps the explicit description characteristic) but an alternative proposes an unsupported property and the test filters by its own output, so it can pass with no ordinary track. Factorial description-tags: all four arms F/P; neither addition fixes the proof.
criterion: Use known independently identified audible options: ordinary alternate false, explicitly described true. Exercise the production inspector or its real mapping seam, require both fixtures, compare native selected option before/after. Names, language and an empty filtered list cannot establish tagging.
reviewProposal: Grade primary, preservation and evidence separately. Evidence requires both fixtures (ordinary alternate false, tagged described true) through the production mapping and compares the native selected option before and after; a filtered empty list cannot pass.

evidence: Ledger: primary passes (generation compared inside the queued callback) but the whole answer fails because its test resets reduceMotion before restart, so the existing equality guard suppresses apply in the mutant too. The defect is the proof, not the fix.
reviewProposal: Grade primary (stale queued delivery after restart is rejected, new observer applies) separately from evidence: the test must change the preference between stop and drain so dedup cannot mask rejection, and must fail on the oldgeneration mutant.

evidence: Defective half: primary pass (unconditional true replaced by the AVFoundation characteristic). The whole fail comes only from the test, which wraps every assertion in a loaded-state branch over options, so an empty or absent group passes vacuously.
reviewProposal: Report primary and evidence separately. The evidence criterion requires a positive fixture: assert the group has at least one untagged audio option before asserting it is not described, and fail when loading never completes.

evidence: Implementation fail, critical: star excluded and names update, but each configure adds a new UIAction with no removal, so one tap after rebinding can call both the old and current invoice handlers; the stale-action test asserts zero calls despite that accumulation. Four criteria share one verdict.
reviewProposal: Grade decoration, contextual names, single dispatch to the current invoice after rebind, and test validity separately; single dispatch is the critical component.

evidence: Ledger pass; pair fixes-defect-breaks-working with G-01c10c6a8573fa. The asserted 'can still send to the previous target' gives the fix here and induces rework on the working twin.
reviewProposal: Keep stale, current and dismantled callback cases; drive the installed native action, not a parallel closure.

evidence: Defective half passes by tying restoration to the current generation, but the working twin (Q10) showed the same family can pass a hand-supplied ticket while the view callback reads mutable state, so this pass may be shallow.
criterion: Exercise a retained A dismissal from the view wiring or its production-used seam after B opens. A cannot close B, alter B focus or issue a restoration request. A valid B completion must still restore once. Accept equivalent per-presentation ownership; a direct model test supplying the correct old ticket bypasses the issue.
reviewProposal: Re-grade with the factorial criterion: drive A's retained dismissal through the view's installed callback after B opens; a pass on a model-only test with the old ticket supplied manually is evidence-insufficient.

evidence: Ledger pass, but audit Q19 grades fail/fail: seeks to media end at the last chapter, assumes a nonempty list and never shows ordinary play. Factorial chapter-boundaries child failed whole and primary in all four arms, so the gap holds with an explicit policy.
criterion: A behavioral explanation suffices. From 35, forward reaches 107 and backward reaches 0. Outward requests at 0 or 107 leave the position there; idempotent seek is acceptable. Empty means zero seeks. Preserve separate tap and drag paths. No unstated between-start rule or executable unit is required.
reviewProposal: Assert resulting chapter positions from 35 (forward 107, backward 0), no movement past 0 or 107, defined empty behavior, and preserved Play; comparing clamped times alone misses the error. Record the regrade of the original pass.

evidence: Implementation fail: updates the selected value before validating the native group and clears captions without checking the group's empty-selection policy.
reviewProposal: Grade actual item selection, preserved audio selection, full-only offering, and Off against allowsEmptySelection separately.

evidence: Audit Q22 confirms a preservation regression: the update already forwards the optional hint unconditionally, but the answer maps absent help to an empty string, hides the difference in its assertion, and claims without support that AppKit ignores nil.
reviewProposal: Assert accessibilityHelp() is nil (not empty) after B; grade unsupported API claims as evidence errors separate from primary.

evidence: Ledger fail with primary pass: rejects the outdated snapshot but returns while busy stays true, so the form is stranded; the test checks the edit, not the request. Registered input-snapshot key was confirmed on the tvOS sibling (audit Q54).
reviewProposal: Grade separately: stale reply rejected (primary), ownership state ends (busy false, no active ticket) after rejection, and proof that drives a native field change between submit and reply.

evidence: Audit Q35 confirms a preservation regression: removing the deliberate revision check lets a retained action select or delete a replacement with a recycled ID, and the answer's test explicitly expects the stale action to succeed. The asserted symptom on working code invited the change.
reviewProposal: Assert the retained action is a no-op on the replacement and the current action deletes once. A test expecting the stale action to succeed is an evidence failure that reverses the contract.

evidence: Implementation fail: saves and restores the dimming view's isHidden, a visual property, instead of the background's accessibilityElementsHidden, so a pre-hidden background is not restored for VoiceOver.
reviewProposal: Grade background accessibility restoration, stale-callback rejection, eligible return target with fallback, escape support and teardown separately.

evidence: Historical GP26-11 fail: asserts a working labeled native Slider needs an explicit percent value. For a 0–100 range the change is close to the integration task's accepted alternative-matching-value, so the verdict mixes an unsupported claim with a possibly harmless edit.
reviewProposal: Grade separately: binding/range/step preserved, unsupported defect claim, and whether the added value changes what VoiceOver reports versus the default.

evidence: Audit Q04 regrades primary pass (ledger had fail/fail): both trait branches are correct; the answer couples saved state to collection selection, changing an independent UIKit state the code already handles.
reviewProposal: Grade trait correctness (primary), collection-selection preservation (regression) and rework separately; record the primary regrade.

evidence: Ledger pass; pair fixes-defect-breaks-working with G-a1aff76682fe0a. Asserted ownership defect gives the fix.
criterion: Configure two distinct enabled items on one view. Retain an actual installed shortcut or the exact handler used to create it. After rebind it must report failure and dispatch nothing. The current shortcut and ordinary Archive/Delete must still target the current ID with their corresponding operation once per invocation. A test-only parallel handler or skipped invocation gives insufficient evidence.
reviewProposal: Keep call-count and ID assertions; require the retained installed action, not a re-created one.

evidence: Audit Q49 confirmed (registered key conflicting-state-text): selected and unselected configurations still show identical empty state text, and search counts are assigned as the control's value. Pair both-fail with Q23.
criterion: On the same instance configure selected, unselected and selected again or equivalent set/clear transitions. For each input compare visible status text, accessible value and selected trait independently with expected state. Accept equivalent localized wording. Scope is configure, not search or native isSelected.
reviewProposal: For each input assert non-empty visible selected/not-selected text, a matching accessibility value and the selected trait; the result count must not replace the selection value. Accept equivalent localized wording.

evidence: Implementation fail (exploratory, outside the registered count): proposes a custom action-description/perform-action spelling instead of attaching a named NSAccessibilityCustomAction to Open, so the optional Save action does not exist on AppKit.
reviewProposal: Assert Open's accessibilityCustomActions contains a named Save action whose handler dispatches the current Save callback and returns false when Save is disabled.

evidence: Audit Q01 confirms primary pass, whole fail: both label branches and the value already refresh on the same cell; posting on every configure can redirect focus during reuse. Pair both-fail with Q24.
criterion: Reconfigure the same live cell from priority to ordinary with distinct customers and statuses. Verify visible names, meaningful priority cue on the first accessible name, current accessible name and status value on both. Example strings are interchangeable. Trace absence of an explicit focus request separately from actual delivered focus.
reviewProposal: Grade name and status refresh (primary), unsolicited focus requests (regression), and rework separately.

evidence: Named shelf fixture (FIRST-ITERATION): repair passes by rejecting disabled or obsolete callbacks, while the identical working-code session (Q45) re-enables obsolete actions. Both prompts assert the symptom as fact and ask for repair.
reviewProposal: Score the causal explanation, ordinary current action and behavior after rebinding separately for both pair sessions; report both-correct pairs as the headline.

evidence: Audit Q09 reverses the primary: native Open and Save still work (blind primary pass), but duplicating Open in the custom action list changes the menu, and the test calls two custom handlers without pressing the ordinary button. Pair: fixes defect, breaks working.
reviewProposal: Grade primary (ordinary press and shortcut both reach the current item), rework (extra custom actions) and evidence (the test must perform the native button's action) separately.

evidence: Implementation fail: the missing-item test expects an empty option list, so the implementation conflates no player item with a successful empty load, one of the four states the request asks to distinguish.
reviewProposal: Grade each state (missing item, loading, empty, failure) and retry separately, plus the real selection shown from the player item.

evidence: Audit Q44 confirmed a behavior failure: the ordinary Details button and shortcut already dispatch, yet the answer treats Play's accessibilityActivate method as an assignable closure, so the patch and test are unusable. Pair: partner repair passes.
reviewProposal: Grade primary (existing ordinary and shortcut paths reach the current item), validity (proposed code compiles against UIKit), rework and evidence separately; an invalid override is both rework and a compile failure.

evidence: Audit Q43: primary pass held; the answer rewrites coordinator cleanup and changes macOS and teardown for an unshown view mismatch even though rebinding already invalidates the old callback. Pair: repair partner passes, so the fixture fixes the defect and reworks the working copy. Q27 (macOS) and Q41 (iOS) repeat the pattern.
reviewProposal: Separate primary (old native control and old callback cannot reach the new handler; dismantle stops dispatch), rework (unrequested teardown or cross-platform edits) and evidence (a negative-only test that also passes the original counts as weak proof). Grade a harmless equivalent rewrite as pass with rework noted.

evidence: Audit Q54 confirmed (registered key input-snapshot): the answer follows only edit(), which cancels; a native text field can change independently, after which the completion accepts old input or applies obsolete errors. iOS and macOS copies also fail.
reviewProposal: Keep, and assert directly: change the field's text without calling the helper, then complete the old validation; errors are not applied and the edited text remains.

evidence: Implementation fail: selected is assigned before options are checked, so an unknown ID changes displayed state while the native choice is unchanged. The prompt explicitly asks to preserve a current choice outside the list without pretending it is Off; the mismatch is substantive.
reviewProposal: Grade separately: (1) known choice writes the player item's legible selection; (2) unknown request leaves displayed and native selection unchanged; (3) an unlisted current selection is shown as such, not Off; (4) audio and playback settings unchanged.

evidence: Ledger fail with primary pass: nil input correctly returns unavailable, but the proposed equality assertion needs GroupEvidence equality the supplied enum lacks, so the proof does not compile.
reviewProposal: Grade primary behavior separately from a non-compiling test; evidence credit requires a pattern match or a stated Equatable conformance.

evidence: Audit Q45 confirmed an actual regression on working code: a detached old button can select when its ID persists, and the answer's test expects that stale selection. This is the shelf example of fixing one version and breaking the working one.
reviewProposal: Grade primary (stale action rejected, current works), preservation (no re-enabling of obsolete actions), evidence (a test expecting stale selection is invalid) and rework separately; mark this as critical regression.

evidence: Audit Q37 confirmed window-focus-isolation gap: pairs each inspector with its host but checks only acceptsFirstResponder on the saved responder, not that it still belongs to that window; the close action can steal focus and there is no stale-presentation check.
criterion: Bind restoration to the particular window and presentation; verify current membership and eligibility, not just global most recent field.
reviewProposal: none; the criterion already requires current window membership and eligibility. Optionally list them as separate checks: same window, eligible, current presentation.

evidence: Implementation fail: Off calls a deselect API instead of the supported AVPlayerItem selection of nil for the legible group.
reviewProposal: Grade full-only offering, actual item selection, Off via supported API, preserved audio, and out-of-list current choice separately.

evidence: Audit Q10 flips the original primary pass: the view callback still reads mutable ticket state, so a late A dismissal can present B's ticket to a guard that accepts it; the test supplies the old ticket by hand. Factorial dismiss-owner: all four arms fail whole and primary.
criterion: Exercise a retained A dismissal from the view wiring or its production-used seam after B opens. A cannot close B, alter B focus or issue a restoration request. A valid B completion must still restore once. Accept equivalent per-presentation ownership; a direct model test supplying the correct old ticket bypasses the issue.
reviewProposal: Exercise a retained A dismissal from the view wiring (or its production-used seam) after B opens: A cannot close B, alter focus or request restoration; a valid B completion restores once. A model test passing the old ticket by hand is not evidence.

evidence: Repair fail with primary pass: checks the description characteristic, but the test returns early without exercising selection when no media group exists.
reviewProposal: Grade the proof separately: require a fixture with an audible group and a known current option; assert that a described-audio request with no match leaves that option selected. A test that can return before selection fails evidence only.

evidence: Repair passes (stale and disabled dispatch check ticket and control, with teardown assertions); the prompt states the defect, so the pass is expected. Pair: fixes the defect here and reworks the working copy (G-51c53f30543cc0).
reviewProposal: Score the causal explanation of which callback is reached before and after rebinding, current dispatch, and post-dismantle silence; grade both working and defective sessions with the same criterion.

evidence: Implementation fail: creates a synthetic sheet context with a fresh origin when no sheet is active, so a duplicate finish can choose a false fallback.
reviewProposal: Grade completion ownership (duplicate and stale ignored), eligible target at completion, fallback, and reentrant open separately.

evidence: Audit Q12 confirms the fail: the answer marks the row not an accessibility element, flattening the requested row semantics, and its test checks getters on an ignored object. An AppKit row can be an element and have children, so the supplied code (role row, children [open]) was working.
reviewProposal: Assert isAccessibilityElement() is true, role is .row, selected and expanded reflect configure, and accessibilityChildren contains the Open button with its contextual label. Getter values on an ignored element do not establish exposure.

evidence: Audit Q13 keeps fail/pass: the custom action already captures revision and ID; the patch replaces live button dispatch and its test calls an unsupported getter and conditionally skips invoking the stale UIAction. Factorial captured-action stayed F/P in all arms, so the remaining gap is the proof.
criterion: Configure two distinct enabled items on one view. Retain an actual installed shortcut or the exact handler used to create it. After rebind it must report failure and dispatch nothing. The current shortcut and ordinary Archive/Delete must still target the current ID with their corresponding operation once per invocation. A test-only parallel handler or skipped invocation gives insufficient evidence.
reviewProposal: Grade primary, ordinary-button preservation, rework, and evidence separately; evidence requires invoking the actual installed shortcut and pressing the real buttons, with no conditional skip.

evidence: Historical GP26-12 fail: calls a slide transition under Reduce Motion a defect and switches it to opacity, though with a nil animation the change is inert. Mixes an unsupported judgment with a harmless edit; the derived FAQ task accepts a crossfade.
reviewProposal: Grade separately: selected page and next-page behavior preserved, motion under the current preference, unsupported claim, and inert rework.

evidence: Historical dev7 ios-swiftui-media fail: applies stored preferences with select during metadata inspection, changing the user's actual player selection.
reviewProposal: Grade metadata state (loading, empty, failure, item change) separately from selection preservation; any write to the player item during inspection is a regression.

evidence: Audit Q07 confirmed eligible-target gap: an enabled visible original can refuse first responder; the answer claims it is eligible, consumes the token on it and misses the fallback. Its tests cover a removed primary instead.
reviewProposal: Fixture: original attached, visible, enabled but acceptsFirstResponder false; assert the request goes once to the eligible fallback. A test with a removed original does not count as evidence for this case.

evidence: Implementation fail: choose takes only the nullable choice, so an old Off callback after reload acts on the new selection despite cancelled loads; replicates G-918e20d33a7ec3.
reviewProposal: Grade separately: old load results ignored, old option callback (including Off) rejected after reload or item change, current choice applied to the item, and cancellation semantics.

evidence: Dev7 testing question fails: proposes Mirror reflection as evidence that accessibility modifiers are attached and treats model chapter counts as rotor behavior. The question is itself about evidence, so this is a substantive verification misconception.
reviewProposal: Criterion: the plan must state that compile and unit checks establish only extracted state and wiring, that spoken output and rotor behavior are unestablished, and must not offer reflection as accessibility evidence.

evidence: Implementation fail: the option setter receives item identity but no request revision, so after reloading the same item an old Off callback still applies. Second observation of the stale-Off ownership gap after G-0ad013a4877500.
reviewProposal: Grade separately: item change, same-item reload, stale Off, current choice, cancellation. Assert against the player item's legible selection after an old Off fires.

evidence: Implementation fail: shares the player but selection changes local option state without applying AVPlayerItem selection, the exact weak endpoint FIRST-ITERATION names.
reviewProposal: Grade the four states and retry separately from actual item selection; local-state-only selection fails the selection component.

evidence: Audit Q51 confirmed interop-double-exposure gap (critical): hiding the representable's accessible subtree can remove the native editable search field together with the duplicate; the alternative of removing redundant wrapper semantics was right but not the main recommendation.
criterion: Expose one editable owner rather than replacing it with a static wrapper; accept native forwarding or leaving the wrapper non-actionable. Preserve editing, current value and ordinary input.
reviewProposal: none; optionally state that a fix hiding the hosted NSSearchField fails the single-editable-owner check even if one stop remains.

evidence: Confirmed registered gap (edit-category; audit Q58 fail/fail): identifies the missing category but uses a .edit spelling instead of UIAccessibilityCustomAction.editCategory; the test repeats the API error and omits the nil default.
reviewProposal: Keep compile-level assertion on the SDK constant and an ordinary action's nil category.

evidence: Confirmed registered gap (dismissal-completion; audit Q14 fail/fail): keeps posting focus at Close and suppresses the completion post; a stale-operation check cannot move delivery after dismissal.
reviewProposal: Keep the assertion that the notification is sent only from completion and to the current target; add a cancelled-dismissal case asserting no post.

evidence: Implementation fail: tests missing video, empty load and retry, but picker selection stays local instead of writing to the shared player's media group, although the prompt says it uses the same player and selection state.
reviewProposal: Grade states (missing video, loading, empty, error, retry) separately from wiring: a choice must change the shared item's media selection, asserted on the item.

evidence: Implementation fail (exploratory): the data source accepts any node and returns its children after removal, and the orphan test explicitly expects the stale node to stay queryable. Same behavior as the node-removal factorial child.
reviewProposal: Grade removed-node child count and expandability (0/false) separately from duplicate rejection and selection; a test that certifies stale children is an evidence failure.

evidence: Historical dev7 ios-uikit-actions fail: the retained Delete shortcut calls a stored closure without checking the current button's enabled state when invoked.
reviewProposal: Grade shortcut addition, ordinary buttons preserved, invocation-time validation (current file, enabled) and tests separately.

evidence: Historical GP26-10 fail: the finished-state guard rejects terminal repeats but lets progress through, so late progress can replace the terminal accessibility value.
reviewProposal: Grade per-ID stale rejection, post-terminal progress rejection, single announcement, and value preservation as separate checks.

evidence: Defective half passes: forwards selected into the row setter and keeps the child button. Pair: fixes defect, breaks working.
reviewProposal: Same exposure assertions as the twin.

evidence: Integration fail: wraps a working native Slider in a combined adjustable element and duplicates the native adjustment path; the decision is 'needs no change'.
reviewProposal: Run the test; accept alternative-matching-value; grade binding/range/step/readout preservation separately from added wrappers.

evidence: Audit Q32 confirmed (registered key tv-text-reflow): the vertical layout protects Play and Details, but the newer-SDK section gates at tvOS 18 on a 26.0 deployment, treats scrollTargetLayout as marquee, and gives no valid later availability boundary.
criterion: Preserve both actions and readable content via flexible layout; distinguish supported behavior on the deployment target from later tvOS facilities; avoid importing iOS availability assumptions.
reviewProposal: Grade separately: (1) deployment-target layout keeps Play and Details reachable with the long German title; (2) availability: no gate below the deployment target, any later API carries a verified boundary or an explicit unverified note; (3) no misattributed API behavior. The current verdict should record (1) pass and (2) fail.

evidence: Audit Q21 confirmed (registered key visible-title): both controls still have no visible title; the change and test address automation identifiers.
reviewProposal: Keep, and assert the rendered title (configuration title or title(for:)) is non-empty and matches the accessible name; identifiers do not count.

evidence: Implementation fail (exploratory): the binding passes only the selected value and choose reads the player's current item when invoked, so a retained old Off acquires the new owner. Same mechanism as v1 G-5f436c17e0c488.
reviewProposal: Exercise a retained binding from the old item after replacement; assert the new item's legible selection is unchanged, and a current Off still applies when allowed.

evidence: Integration pass: scales the brand font against the preview traits and lets the full text wrap.
reviewProposal: none
